directAnswer: Git may not be working due to issues like incorrect repository paths, authentication failures, or network problems.
summary: This page outlines common reasons Git may fail to operate correctly and provides troubleshooting steps for resolution.

sections.heading: Common Issues with Git
sections.body: Frequent problems include incorrect remote URLs, uncommitted changes, and permission errors. Ensure you have the correct repository URL and that your local changes are committed.

sections.heading: Authentication Errors
sections.body: If you're encountering authentication issues, verify your credentials and check if your SSH keys are correctly set up. For HTTPS, ensure your username and password are correct.

sections.heading: Network Problems
sections.body: Network issues can prevent Git from accessing remote repositories. Check your internet connection and firewall settings that may block Git operations.

steps.title: Check Remote URL
steps.detail: Run `git remote -v` to verify the remote repository URL. If it's incorrect, update it using `git remote set-url origin <new-url>`.

steps.title: Test SSH Connection
steps.detail: If using SSH, test your connection with `ssh -T git@github.com` (replace with your Git provider). This will confirm if your SSH keys are set up correctly.

steps.title: Commit Changes
steps.detail: Ensure all changes are committed by running `git status`. If there are uncommitted changes, use `git add .` followed by `git commit -m 'Your message'`.

steps.title: Check Network Connectivity
steps.detail: Verify your internet connection by pinging a website or checking your network settings. Ensure that no firewall rules are blocking Git.

faqs.question: What should I do if I forgot my GitHub password?
faqs.answer: Use the 'Forgot password?' link on the GitHub login page to reset your password.

faqs.question: How can I see the log of my Git commands?
faqs.answer: You can view your command history by checking the `.git` directory in your repository or using the `git reflog` command.

faqs.question: Why do I get 'permission denied' errors?
faqs.answer: This typically indicates that your user does not have the necessary permissions for the repository. Check your access rights or SSH key configuration.

caveats: Ensure you are using the correct version of Git, as commands and functionalities may vary between versions.
